newsitem.title: NORWAY: N.Hydro ups Troll oil reserves to 1.2 bln barrels.
newsitem.headline: N.Hydro ups Troll oil reserves to 1.2 bln barrels.

text.p: Norsk Hydro ASA said on Wednesday it had upgraded recoverable oil reserves at the North Sea Troll field to 1.17 billion barrels from one billion barrels.
The figures include the Troll B and planned Troll C oil developments.

"The main rea increase in recoverable reserves are improved drilling technology and increased cost efficiency," Thor Tangen, Vice President for the Troll project, said at a news conference at the 1996 Offshore Northern Seas conference.

"Costs have been halved by the industrialisation of production instead of having tailor-made units for each function. Also seismic and drilling technology are allowing us to go exactly where we want to go."

The Troll B platform came onstream in September 1995 and pumped an average 249,569 barrels per day (bpd) in July. Troll C is planned to start up in September 1999 at a rate of 20,000 cubic metres per day, or 125,800 bpd.
